title: Binary Search Target
statement: Given a sorted array nums and target, return true if target exists.
think: What is the task asking? Given a sorted array nums and target, return true if target exists.
What is the key operation? Identify the repeated action over the input.
What wording signals stand out? In Spot wording signals, look for sorted array/list, find target, existence vs position, O(log n), and halving the search space each step.
What is the brute force idea? Use extra loops or repeated checks.
What is the better/optimal idea? Use a clean binary search solution.
What are the edge cases? Empty array, single element, and boundaries.
What is the complexity? Time O(log n) and O(1) extra space for binary search on a sorted array.
How would I explain it in an interview? State the pattern, the key operation, and the complexity.
interview: I would solve it using Binary Search. I would first identify the core operation, then apply a simple binary search approach and mention the complexity.

whyThisPattern: This is a Binary Search problem when the data is ordered so you can discard half the candidates each step: see Spot wording signals for English phrasing (sorted, find target, O(log n), etc.).
whyNotOtherPatterns: Not Linear Scan, because sorted input allows a faster logarithmic search.
Not HashSet, because ordered boundaries matter.
